startup.name: Interfaze
startup.one_liner: AI model built for high accuracy deterministic tasks
startup.description: A model that combines specialized CNN and DNN models with transformers for tasks needing consistent output such as document extraction, object detection, classification and audio understanding. Sold as an API. Five person team with an architecture paper and public benchmarks. Batch Spring 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test note: the company was accepted, so this is an if accepted view. A blind prior starts near 1 percent, and the factors in the YC acceptance table are applied loosely here. Not part of the scored test.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC might decline because the claim to beat frontier models on benchmarks the company chose is easy to doubt, and document extraction is crowded with funded startups and cloud giants. Interviewers may see no clear buyer or revenue and a wedge that general models improve into.

anchors.source: Ran python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only: seed 49 / 59 / 65 percent (lower, known, upper), series A 13 / 15 / 29 with cond 26 percent (n=74), series B cond 16 percent (n=19), series C cond 0 percent (n=3, too small). Broad cohort also checked with --industry B2B --years 2018-2021: seed cond 81, A cond 32, B cond 39, C cond 57 percent.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Set above the 59 percent anchor because a five person team with a research paper and open benchmarks in AI infrastructure is the kind that raised quickly in 2025 and 2026. The seed step here means a round above the standard 500K YC deal within about 12 months, and the anchor is for any seed ever, so the 12 month window pulls it down while a hot category pushes it up.

bands.rationale: Small round just above the YC check, mostly angels, if traction is thin.

ladder.why_it_fails: A round above the YC check fails if developers try the API and stay on cheaper frontier models, or if benchmark wins are not reproduced on customers' own documents. Analogs like pulse-3 and extend raised only with paying customers, so an AI infrastructure story without revenue could stall.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if usage stays low volume and pricing falls with token costs. Frontier labs add structured outputs and cheaper vision models every quarter, and the narrow accuracy edge may close before the company builds a moat in customer data or workflows. Peers in document AI such as pulse-3, extend and veryfi-inc show that revenue and customer references, not benchmark scores alone, decide who raises the next round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely failure is that general models and cloud document services catch up on accuracy and drive price down, so a small team cannot defend margin. An acquisition by a larger AI platform for the team and model is a common middle result. Peers in document AI such as pulse-3, extend and veryfi-inc show that revenue and customer references, not benchmark scores alone, decide who raises the next round.

killers.risk: Frontier models and cloud services close the accuracy gap
killers.evidence: Mistral OCR, Google Document AI and Gemini vision all improve and cut price, and benchmark vendors disagree on rankings.
killers.mitigation: Focus on determinism and per customer fine tuning.

killers.risk: Benchmarks chosen by the company do not convince buyers
killers.evidence: Most OCR benchmarks are vendor authored and failure rate or determinism is rarely measured independently.
killers.mitigation: Offer bake offs on customer documents.

killers.evidence: Reported per page prices range widely, from near zero to several dollars per thousand pages.
killers.mitigation: Move up to workflows and vertical solutions.

killers.risk: Unclear go to market for a general model across many tasks
killers.evidence: The description spans documents, objects and audio with no single buyer.
killers.mitigation: Pick one wedge such as document extraction.

technical_complexity.rationale: Merging specialized vision and audio models with transformers into one API that is accurate and consistent needs real research and training data, which the paper suggests the team has. A five person team can build a competitive document model but scaling across many tasks is hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Labs and cloud vendors already ship OCR and structured extraction, and a well funded rival could match the accuracy in a few quarters. Incentive is high since document processing is a large enterprise workload.

evidence.claim: Enterprises pay for document processing, with many vendors competing on accuracy and price per thousand pages.
Accuracy and consistency are open problems across vendors and not independently benchmarked.

roadmap.goal: Show independent evidence of the accuracy edge.
Convert API trials to paying usage.

Become infrastructure standard for deterministic AI.

pros.evidence: The YC text links an arXiv paper and public leaderboards.

pros.evidence: Many funded vendors and cloud services compete in this market.

brand.name: Interfaze
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Interfaze" --era 2022+ gave invented or proper noun, 9 characters, 3 syllables.
strengths: Short invented name with an interface connotation
weaknesses: Spelling with z may be mistaken and it is not self explanatory
brand.rationale: Invented names are the largest group in the name tables with no outcome penalty. It suggests an interface to models, which fits an API, and it is easy to say.

narrative.headline: Technically credible team in a crowded but real market, likely to raise a seed and then face commoditization pressure.
narrative.general_summary: Interfaze is an API model for deterministic tasks such as document extraction. A research paper and open benchmarks make it a good fit for fast AI infrastructure seeds in 2026. The risk is commoditization: cloud services and frontier models keep improving, benchmarks are vendor authored and customers can switch easily. The document AI analogs show the category funds a few winners and leaves others small. A seed is likelier than not, Series A is roughly one in three and the base case is a small acquisition or a narrower pivot.

assumptions: Blind test: only the YC listing text was used for the company itself.
Seed means more than 500K within about 12 months of batch start; cohort anchors are for any seed ever.
Recent batches are right censored in the base rates.
Web results dated after the batch start were ignored.
